name: Vine Temptress
body:
Vine Temptress
CR 3

This nude, young woman seems a little out of place, but only for a moment. Soon, you find yourself lost in her smile and admiring her body, suited exactly to your tastes.

XP 800
N Medium plant
Init +2; Senses low-light vision; Perception +2

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 13, flat-footed 13 (+1 dodge, +2 Dex, +3 natural)
hp 37 (5d8+15)
Fort +7, Ref +3, Will +3
DR 5/slashing; Immune plant traits; Resist cold 10, fire 10

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee slam +4 (1d4+1)
Special Attacks detonate, energy drain (1 level, DC 16)

STATISTICS

Str 13, Dex 15, Con 16, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 19
Base Atk +3; CMB +4; CMD 16
Feats Dodge, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Diplomacy)
Skills Diplomacy +12, Disguise +9 (+29 to appear as target’s race)
Languages any one (see below)
SQ custom made, tethered

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Custom Made (Ex)

Each vine temptress is spawned in response to a single humanoid creature and created only to attract it. It gains a +20 bonus on disguise checks to appear as a member of its target’s race, a +4 insight bonus on diplomacy checks against its target and the ability to speak one language of its target.

Detonate (Su)

As a full-round action, a vine temptress can explode in a violent burst of blinding energy. This kills the vine temptress and destroys its body, dealing 5d6 force damage to every creature in a 20 ft. radius and blinding them for 1d6 rounds. A DC 15 Reflex save halves this damage and negates the blinded condition. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Energy Drain (Su)

A vine temptress drains energy from a willing, living creature it lures into a prolonged act of passion with a duration of at least 1 minute. A creature cannot be subject to this energy drain more than once per day, regardless of how many acts of passion with the temptress it accepts.

Tethered (Su)

A vine temptress is connected to its creator by a thin, invisible, incorporeal cord, allowing it to move up to 100 feet per Hit Dice (500 feet for most vine temptresses) from the center of the clearing. The vine has AC 22 and 10 hit points. Severing the cord instantly kills the vine temptress, but doesn’t harm the attractor fungus.

ECOLOGY

Environment any underground
Organization solitary, pair, or colony (3-250)
Treasure standard

The biggest danger of vine temptresses comes from their creator and master, an attractor fungus. It is debatable if these creatures are themselves intelligent, or their malign will is instead a highly evolved, but non-sapient feeding scheme. An attractor fungus is a pulsating, fleshy sac of malleable and wet fungal mass 10 inches in diameter, riddled with brightly glowing, membrane-covered holes. It is immobile and often lies dozens of feet underground. No plants larger than shrubs grow within 200 feet of the attractor fungus, and when encountered in forests, such clearings make for enticing campsites or resting points for people traveling through the area.

Humanoids that enter this area must succeed at a DC 22 Will save or be subject to an overwhelming urge to stay there and set up camp, and on subsequent days, a growing aversion to the thought of leaving this peaceful place. This works as a curse mimicking the sympathy spell. This effect is permanent and can only be removed by break enchantment or a stronger spell, or by forcibly transporting the affected creature at least 1000 feet from the attractor fungus.

Every day, the fungus can create a single vine temptress within 100 feet from itself.

The vine temptress is rapidly assembled from magically conjured plant matter and becomes active after 1 minute. This process is most often done at night, to minimize the possibility of someone witnessing it. Each vine temptress is created specifically to seduce one of the cursed humanoids and resembles a physically attractive member of the target’s race. Despite their name, vine temptresses can be of any gender and assume the form of the gender their target is sexually attracted to. Vine temptresses created to seduce humanoids shielded from thought detection (for example by mind blank) speak Common, have no insight bonus to Diplomacy checks against their target and appear as male to seduce female-looking humanoids and female to seduce male-looking humanoids. Each vine temptress is made wholly of plant matter that perfectly mimics flesh. Seeing the truth requires a DC 37 Perception check or a close examination with a Heal check.

A newly created vine temptress approaches its target and focuses its attentions on luring it into life-draining sexual activities. This energy serves as a food source and nourishment for the attractor fungus and is transmitted through the incorporeal cord with which it creates and controls the temptresses. The vine temptresses are unaware of their creator and feel only intense affection towards their target, caring little for other people or the world beyond the clearing. They are not evil and don’t register as such, allowing the attractor fungus to better trick its prey. On rare occasions, a target may escape the curse but remain in love with the vine temptress.

These couples often try to escape the vile place, but such plans always fail when the temptress reaches the end of its invisible tether, severing it and dying on the spot, turning into a pile of inanimate plant matter instantly. The same happens when their actions drain all life from their victim, as the attractor fungus has no use for minions created to seduce a dead creature and withdraws the animating force immediately.

Cursed humanoids are unaware of any energy drain bestowed by engaging in acts of passion with vine temptresses and their attitudes towards them are automatically friendly when they first approach. These effects are results of the curse, but both can be dispelled separately (CL 12th) and are treated as modify memory and charm monster respectively. While vine temptresses aren’t dangerous combatants, all of them have the ability to detonate the magic that sustains them. This kills the temptress, and as such the ability is rarely used, most often when their target is under attack and hopeless. It matters little to the temptress if the attacker is a genuine threat, or just its target’s ally that avoided the curse and now desperately tries to take their friend out of the cursed clearing and their murderous lover’s arms.

There are no known limits to how many vine temptresses an attractor fungus can create and operate at once, but it always creates only a single one for every cursed humanoid on the clearing. For larger groups, it may take months before everyone has their lover, at which point many of those targeted earlier may be dead already, their companions giving little thought to this tragedy, entirely occupied with their own partners.

An attractor fungus has 50 hit points, though it dies in 1d6 rounds after being brought wholly out of the earth or into the area of natural sunlight. Destroying the attractor fungus should award an amount of XP determined by the GM, with the suggested amount being equal to a CR 10 encounter.
